messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: MARINER_RESERVED_POOL_LATENCY 
Tenant: mariner, pool: reserved-eu-west-1a, metric: p95_latency_tokens, threshold: 500ms, current: 1.2s

pagerduty: PD-INC-4721 created and paged oncall schedule (priority: P1). Escalation timer started.

Asha (oncall): acked — I'm investigating. @Maya can you join for customer comms if needed? :eyes:

Maya: on my way, pulling graphs now.

Asha (oncall): Summary so far: 5xxs are not spiking, it's latency only. Affected routes: /v1/generate (mariner-prod key). p95 token latency jumped ~5x at 14:03 UTC. No deploys in last 12h per deploy-bot.

Mike: looking at reserved pool dashboard — queue depth for mariner pool up, workers at 100% GPU utilization on a subset of nodes. Might be a localized hot shard.

SRE-Bridge: linking perf traces: https://console.redwood.internal/trace/PD-4721?view=tenant

Asha (oncall): Running quick checks:
```
# check pool health
kubectl -n reserved-mariner get pods -l tenant=mariner -o wide
kubectl -n reserved-mariner top pods | sort -k3 -r | head -n 10
```

Mike: found one pod with abnormally high iowait and GPU memory fragmentation (node eu-west-1a-23). Pod: mariner-reserved-7c9b. Attempting rolling restart of that pod now.

Asha (oncall): go for it. Note: we should avoid full pool drain if possible — prefer single pod restart.

Mike: restarted pod mariner-reserved-7c9b. Post-restart logs show lots of KV cache evictions and a flurry of long requests while warmup happens:
```
[2026-03-15T14:08:12Z] INFO kv_cache: evicting prefix cache size=0->0.1GB
[2026-03-15T14:08:12Z] WARN runtime: attention kernel fallback for model redwood-v2-small
[2026-03-15T14:08:13Z] INFO serve: pgid=mariner req=abcd1234 tokens=512 latency=1.1s
```

Maya: customer impact — we see elevated latencies for 8% of production traffic for mariner keys, errors still <0.1%. Sending heads-up to Customer Success.

pagerduty: Escalation: PD rule advanced to L2 after 10m without full resolution. Paging Ryan (sre@redwood) and oncall list.

Ryan: taking over the incident. quick check: any rate limiting or quota hits?

Asha (oncall): no quota hits. Looks like hot cache/warmup coupled with one noisy pod. Restart reduced latency on that subset but p95 still ~650ms (above 500ms SLO).

Ryan: ok. Two angles: 1) short-term: add burst capacity and temporarily route a percentage of mariner requests to fallback pool (compatible model variant). 2) medium: schedule KV cache pre-warm and bump auto-scaling threshold for reserved pools.

Asha (oncall): agreed. Implementing temporary route rule: 10% traffic -> fallback-reserved-eu-west (lower capacity but lower queue).

SRE-Bridge: applying routing change:
```
# route rule
redwoodctl routing update --tenant mariner --rule "fallback:10%" --from reserved-eu-west-1a --to fallback-eu-west
```

SRE-Bridge: routing change applied. Observability note: expect spike on fallback pool metrics.

Maya: notifying Mariner CS: "We observed transient reserved-pool latency affecting a subset of requests. We've applied a 10% fallback route and restarted a noisy pod. We're monitoring and will follow up with RCA."

Mariner-CS (via DM): thanks, please tell us ETA to full recovery. Customer wants SLA impact estimate.

Asha (oncall): current p95 down from 1.2s to ~480ms on routed traffic, overall p95 for tenant now ~520ms. Still marginally above SLO; keeping watch. ETA for stable <500ms ~ 15–30 minutes if warming continues and no other noisy nodes show up.

Mike: scanning other nodes — another node eu-west-1a-11 shows elevated GPU memory fragmentation. I'm going to cordon and recycle it during low risk window; want to avoid mass restart.

Ryan: approved cordon/recycle of eu-west-1a-11. Coordinate with autoscaler team if HPA adjusts.

Mike: cordoned and drained one workload, respawned new pod on eu-west-1b. New pod shows clean kernel selection (no fallback). p95 across reserved pool now ~460ms.

Asha (oncall): good sign. I'll keep fallback route at 10% for another 10 minutes and then remove if stable.

pagerduty: PD-INC-4721: acknowledged by Asha, escalated to Ryan (L2). Current status: mitigation in progress.

SRE-Bridge: quick post-mit metrics:
- tenant mariner total qps: 120 rps
- reserved-eu-west-1a queue depth: dropped 72% after pod recycle
- fallback-eu-west handled 12 rps (10%)
- p95 tenant latency: 460ms

Maya: customer updated. They asked for root cause and next steps. Suggest we say: likely cache evictions + localized node noise; mitigation: node recycle + short-term routing; next step: RCA with kernel/runtime team for attention-kernel fallbacks.

Asha (oncall): agree. Logging remediation steps into incident tracker.

SRE-Bridge: Would you like me to open an RCA ticket and link traces?

Ryan: yes, open RCA and assign to eng-runtime + mariner oncall. Tag with PD-4721 and include timeline and quick logs.

SRE-Bridge: RCA created: INTERNAL-7321. Added trace links and logs.

Asha (oncall): scaling down the fallback route:
```
redwoodctl routing update --tenant mariner --rule "fallback:0%"
```

SRE-Bridge: fallback removed. Monitoring for 10m.

Maya: customer confirmed degraded experience is resolved for now and appreciates quick action. They want weekly follow-up.

Asha (oncall): moving incident to resolved state in PD after 30m stable. Please add any further notes.

pagerduty: PD-INC-4721 status: RESOLVED by Asha (oncall). Closing page.

Ryan: thanks team. Action items:
- eng-runtime: investigate kernel fallback triggers for redwood-v2-small (assigned INTERNAL-7321).
- infra: evaluate node selection heuristics to avoid putting many mariner pods on same physical host in eu-west-1a.
- devex: add runbook snippet for "reserved pool noisy pod" (pre-warm KV cache guidance).
- CS: follow up with Mariner in 24h.

Mike: noted. I'll add stack-level logs to RCA.

Asha (oncall): handing off to Ryan for longer-term followups. Ryan, you're now incident owner.

Ryan: thanks, taking ownership for postmortem and action tracking. Closing the slack thread in 1h unless more alerts. :white_check_mark:
